dataset_meta.name: Compound-exercise technique reference dataset (10 exercises)
dataset_meta.intended_use: Reference knowledge base for an AI system that compares a person's detected body pose/movement against documented technique cues.
dataset_meta.how_built: Web sources (3 or more per exercise) were read, their technique cues were extracted and paraphrased, and each cue was compared across sources. Every checkpoint lists which sources support it and whether sources agree.

agreement_values.consensus: every source that addresses the point agrees (does not mean every source mentions it)
agreement_values.single_source: only one source I read addresses the point; treat as lower confidence
agreement_values.conflict: sources disagree; the per_source field shows each position and nothing is averaged

read_depth_values.excerpt: only the portions returned by search were read (may be partial)
read_depth_values.excerpt (supplementary): extra source used to add or cross-check detail

important_limitations: These are coaching/instruction texts, not biomechanics measurements. Numeric thresholds exist only where a source stated one; everything else is qualitative. null numeric = no number in the sources.
Fields named detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant are my suggestions for how a cue might map to pose keypoints. They are NOT from the sources and are not validated.
Most sources did not state tolerances (how many degrees of deviation are acceptable). Do not treat expected values as exact pass/fail cut-offs without expert review.
Only the StrongLifts squat and bench press pages were read in full; other exercises are based on excerpts, so 'not_specified_by_sources' lists gaps that may be filled by the full pages.
Several sources are brand/blog content, not peer-reviewed. Some individual claims (e.g., exact angles, 'never do X') are the source author's opinion; conflicts are preserved rather than resolved.
Absolute loads (kg) are mostly not given because they depend on the individual. Where a source gave sets/reps they are listed.
Text is paraphrased from the sources, not quoted. Verify with a qualified coach or physiotherapist before using this as ground truth for health or safety decisions.

global_principles.principle: Neutral spine is required in squat, deadlift, row, plank and lunge (no rounding, no excess arching).
Brace the core/glutes before loading (breath + tension): squat, bench, deadlift, overhead press, curl, plank, dips.
Use a full, controlled range of motion; momentum and partial reps are flagged as errors in most sources.
Technique is individual: several sources say limb length, shoulder width and torso proportions change the exact positions.
Reduce load when form degrades (stated by several sources).

Either high bar (on traps, base of neck) or low bar (between traps and rear delts, top of scapular spine). Bar centered left-right before unracking. High bar: more upright torso, knees more forward. Low bar: more forward lean, more hip involvement.

Medium grip, hands outside shoulders, narrower than bench-press grip. Squeeze the bar but let the upper back, not the hands/wrists, carry the load. Full grip or thumbless both acceptable; thumbless can help wrists.
Elbows down and back, slightly behind the torso at the top; forearms inclined (not vertical, not horizontal). At the bottom elbows stay in line with the torso.
Squeeze shoulder blades together, arch the upper back, raise the chest BEFORE unracking, so lats/upper back form a shelf for the bar.
Head in line with torso. Look at a point on the floor/bottom of the wall ahead. Do not look at the ceiling, feet or sideways.

checkpoints.expected: About mid-chest level so you only straighten the legs to unrack and stay flat-footed (too high forces you onto toes). MasterClass: adjust to your own height.
Horizontal pins set just below the bottom position of the squat (not so high you hit them on good reps, not so low you must lean to reach them).
Put the feet under the bar and stand up straight (not lunge-style, not feet behind the bar).
Short walkout: one step back with each leg (SL) / one or two steps back (BOS). Then lock hips and knees.
Bend hips and knees at the same time: hips back (like sitting on a toilet/chair) while knees push out. Do not only bend the knees; do not only hinge the hips.

Knees stay in line with the feet and push out; do not cave inward. Knees move forward during the first half of the descent then stay while hips keep going down. At the bottom knees end above/almost directly above the toes.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press (flat)
equipment: flat bench ~45 cm (18 in) high, ~30 cm (12 in) wide, rated at least 300 kg (600 lb) incl. body weight (SL)

sources.name: The Barbell - How to Bench Press
Built With Science - Bench press form by anatomy

checkpoints.expected: Lie with eyes under the bar (bar over eyes when looking up). Head neutral; do not push the head into the bench (hair touches bench only).
Shoulder blades squeezed together and down ('pen between them'), chest lifted toward the ceiling, upper back tight, lats squeezed. Shoulders stay back on the bench; do not shrug forward.

SL: natural arch only (a flat hand can slide between lower back and bench), no horseshoe over-arch, butt stays on bench. TB: natural arch, glutes touch bench but carry no weight. BWS: tune arch to your anatomy. FV (powerlifting): larger arch built by driving hips up, pulling blades back/down, lowering hips; flat-foot with feet tucked back increases arch but needs flexibility.
checkpoints.detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant: gap between lumbar and bench in side view

checkpoints.expected: Whole foot flat on floor incl. heels; shoulder-width stance (heel-to-heel), feet under knees or slightly behind; knee and ankle about 90 deg; toes can turn out about 30 deg. TB: heels slightly behind knees; feet in front of knees weakens base. No feet on bench or in the air.

Bar low in the base of the palm over the forearm bones, close to the wrist ('bulldog grip': rotate hands in then close). Wrist, elbow aligned: straight line bar-wrist-elbow. Wrists must not bend back.
Thumbs wrapped around the bar (full grip). No thumbless grip.

SL: pinky just inside the ring marks, whatever gives vertical forearms at the bottom. TB: depends on shoulder width. BWS: choose elbow angle first, then set width to allow it. FV: raw lifters often use the 81 cm maximum legal width but too wide causes shoulder impingement.

checkpoints.expected: Bench 45 cm (18 in) high so hips sit slightly above knees; 30 cm (12 in) wide; load rating >= 300 kg.
Set so arms are still bent when you grab the bar and you straighten them to unrack. Too high: shoulders shrug forward. Too low: you waste strength.
Slightly below chest level so you never touch them on good reps; to fail, lower to chest then flatten the torso onto the pins.
Unrack by straightening the arms with elbows locked, move the bar horizontally until balanced over the shoulder joint BEFORE lowering. Do not lower straight from the uprights.

SL: elbows tucked about 75 deg from torso (upper arm angle), never 90 deg flared (shoulder impingement), never touching torso. BWS: choose the angle that suits your anatomy; lower angle biases upper chest, more flared biases mid/lower chest. FV: should feel natural, too low (toward stomach) reduces power.

numeric.note: SL; angle between upper arm and torso, 'depends on your build'

Controlled but not slow; touch-and-go (SL, no pause) with no bouncing off the chest (brush the shirt). Competition lifts use a pause.

Lock elbows gently (no hyper-extension); bar over shoulder joint.
Lock out, move bar horizontally back against the rack uprights, then bend arms to lower it into the hooks. Do not look at the uprights.

checkpoints.expected: TG: back knee under the hip. CV: hover, do not let the back knee touch the ground (maintain tension). LC: stop when both knees near 90 deg or when the back knee lightly touches the ground briefly.
Front foot/knee point straight forward (knee must not turn inward); rear foot/knee also straight forward (rotating out adds torque).
checkpoints.detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant: knee caving: front knee x medial to ankle x

checkpoints.expected: Torso upright, spine perpendicular to the floor, shoulders back and down, core braced, pelvis level; no forward lean.
checkpoints.detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant: trunk angle vs vertical small and constant

checkpoints.expected: Drive up through the front heel (glutes/hamstrings) and return to standing each rep.

common_errors.correct_instead: Keep knee tracking over the foot
Step longer than a walking stride
Step 1-1.5 foot lengths; land on the heel

common_errors.error: Too much pressure on the front of the foot

checkpoints.expected: Forearms on the floor, elbows directly under the shoulders, upper arms vertical. SH: if the shoulder is behind the elbow you are holding with the shoulders, not the core. TG: elbows too close to the body or too far forward prevents proper core engagement.
checkpoints.detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant: elbow x approx. shoulder x in side view

checkpoints.expected: IH: toes directly under the ankles. MS: feet hip-width apart, toes tucked under. DN: toes tucked under.
Straight line from head/crown to tailbone and heels; shoulders, hips and feet in line.
checkpoints.detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant: shoulder-hip-ankle collinearity in side view

checkpoints.expected: Hips neither sagging nor piked. Dropped hips put the lumbar spine in extension and can cause severe low-back pain (FV); weak abs can make the butt lift (FV).
checkpoints.detection_hint_inferred_by_assistant: hip keypoint y relative to the shoulder-ankle line

checkpoints.expected: Neutral neck: ears over shoulders (FV); gaze at the floor just ahead of the hands (SH, MS); IH: do not look up or tuck the chin to the chest; TG: looking forward/upward breaks neutral spine.

Squeeze glutes and pull the belly toward the spine (IH, MS, DN). FV: tense legs, glutes, chest, shoulders, arms and core. SP: press the elbows into the floor / actively push away from the floor, engage lats.
Breathe steadily; never hold your breath.

IH: 60 s is a good goal. MS: hold as long as form is good; start at 30 s; add 5-10 s; if 60 s is easy do 3x60 s. SH: about 1 minute with proper form; build from 10 s to 20 s. SP: beginners 20-30 s for 3-4 sets; add about 5 s per week; about 2 min is enough; 3-5 sets at 60-90% of max hold with 60 s rest. FV: do not chase very long holds, better ways to train the core.

per_source.MS: as long as form holds; 30 s start; 3x60 s
per_source.SP: 20-30 s x 3-4 sets for beginners, cap ~2 min

checkpoints.expected: Low-back pain during a plank signals bad form, weak abs or poor stability: stop the hold. Shoulder 'burn' is normal (MS).

breathing.text: Never hold your breath; slow steady breathing.

common_errors.correct_instead: Lower hips into the straight line
Keep neck in line with the spine
